info.title: Diagnostics
info.summary: Read-only views of the knowledge bases: where every source and reading came from.

get.description: The view's name, as `configs/app_config.json` holds it under `ui`.

Every work of every knowledge base served: the free catalog in its order, then the licensed works as their
export lists them. Only the free knowledge base has a catalog.

An HTML work (the operator's 6.a): its outline by heading and its sections, from the search index; where the index is
not built, the work says so and names the command.
One section of an HTML work as indexed, its chunks in order with where each stands in the section's text.

The article, chapter or other top unit that holds a section, whole: every section with its original and its
chunks, its dropped headings at their place, in the work's order.

A licensed EPUB work (123.a, the operator's P1.a): its outline by heading and its sections, as the librarian
serves them, each with the count of its images.
One section of a licensed EPUB work: its text in runs, each image where its mark stands, and its neighbours.

An image of a licensed EPUB work by its path inside the EPUB, read from its zip, never extracted; only one its
sections name.

A book's companion code (#12): its folders and files, each file with the core's catalog entry, and the core's
count of its units by category.
One file of a code work as the librarian serves it (#12): its text and lines, its catalog entry, its neighbours.

A read page's chunks in semantic search's index, placed in its quoted blocks by their text (the operator's W4,
21 Nov): the page view's "as served" mode draws them, asked for only when that mode is on.

One judgement of the page shown as it judged (181.a): its reading, read-only, with its findings on the blocks.
`judgement` is the id a page's judgement carries (`<reading key>:<version>:<again>`).

The text the search and the chat quote for the page. Where the export has not cut a book's quoted text on this
machine, the core cuts it on the first call, about a minute for a large one, and keeps it.
Every run of the pipeline, newest first, both knowledge bases together; a base not listed says why.
One run whole: its code version, its cost by provider, and the pages it chose a reading for.
The corpus at a glance (O3.a): a headline summed over the knowledge bases served, and the latest runs.
The pages behind a figure of the overview: every page served that matches every filter given.

Every work of both knowledge bases, how far it is converted and why pages did not pass, as the core counted it;
under --public-only the licensed shelf is never read.
The judge's and stage 2's findings grouped by kind, block class and work, void ones apart, with their pages.

Every version of the reader's and the judge's instructions (148.a): its state, its sha256 now and frozen, why it
was made, its text, and its change from the version before it.

The search server's call log, newest first: who asked what, which pages answered, how long it took. Under
--public-only only the calls that concern the free knowledge base alone, and how many were left out.

The librarian's tools as the running server lists them (L1.a), in its staggered order, each with its description,
a line on what it costs and takes, and its form's fields from its input schema; the page's first call opens its one
session with the librarian. Where the librarian does not answer, it says so in words.

post.description:
One tool call over MCP to the running librarian, as an IDE session makes it, its client named "view": the answer
as it came and its parts for the page. Local only and Origin-checked, since `semantic_search` spends a fraction of a
cent, and a model call with the router on. 503 where the page calls nothing here or the librarian does not answer,
404 for a tool it does not offer, 502 where the call failed on its way; a tool's own error is an answer.

get.description:
Whether a person's verdict is taken here (the app started with --allow-verdicts), the lists its dialog offers in
the core's words, and each knowledge base's background export, which the view follows to reload a page.

post.description:
A person's verdict on the reading a page shows, the one route here that writes (213.b): recorded at once by the
core, append-only, and the export set going in the background. 403 when the app was started without
--allow-verdicts or the request comes from elsewhere; 422 with the core's sentence for an input it refuses.

A person's promotion of a Lab reading to the page's reading (#18), behind the same switch and guard as a verdict:
recorded at once by the core, the export set going. 403 without --allow-verdicts or from elsewhere; 422 with the
core's sentence for anything but a valid page/1 Lab reading of that page.

✦ propose (W2.a): a model's correction of one block, asked of the core with the judge's findings on it, kept by
the core and answered again from its store for free; never recorded by itself. 409 with the core's reason where it
sends nothing; 403 unless the app was started with --allow-verdicts or where the request comes from elsewhere.

A correction's text as the table it would be (204.a's path), for the dialog to show before it is sent; writes
nothing.

AgentPrompt.title: AgentPrompt
AgentPrompt.description: A session's agent prompt by version and hash (#17); `derived` where the core tied it by the agent's own transcript.

AnsweredJudgement.title: AnsweredJudgement
AnsweredJudgement.description:
The judgement a person's verdict answered (#17), by its version, model and date; `derived` where the core assigned
it by time rather than recorded it.

AnsweredJudgementRef.title: AnsweredJudgementRef
AnsweredJudgementRef.description: The judgement a person's verdict answered (#17): its key, version, model, mode, date and verdict.

AnsweredWork.title: AnsweredWork
AnsweredWork.description: A work that answered a search over works (`search_works`, decision 124.a).

AppInfo.title: AppInfo
AppInfo.description:
The name the view shows in its header and its browser tab (decision 149.c): a working name, kept in the app's own
config so it changes in one place, without code.

Attempt.title: Attempt
Attempt.description:
One reading ever bought for a page, as the export lists them, oldest first. Its text stays in the private store;
only the reading the page shows is exported, so the others are shown by their record alone.

AttemptCheck.title: AttemptCheck
AttemptCheck.description: What the check made of one reading: its state, the judge's verdict where it judged, and the check's outcome.

Block.title: Block
Block.description: One block of a reading, in the form the view draws it; which of the body fields is set depends on the class.

CallHead.title: CallHead
CallHead.description: The answer's head line: its state and words, relevance against its floor, how long it took, whether a model ran.

CatalogUnit.title: CatalogUnit
CatalogUnit.description: One unit `code_catalog` lists (#12): its file, what the core's catalog says of it, and its file in this view.

Chosen.title: Chosen
Chosen.description: Why the page's reading was chosen over its others, by which run and when (the pipeline database, 51.a).

ChosenPage.title: ChosenPage
ChosenPage.description: A page one run chose a reading for, and why.

ChunkBlock.title: ChunkBlock
ChunkBlock.description: A quoted block in a chunk, or in none, in its served form: only the part the chunk holds where it holds part of it.

ChunkGroup.title: ChunkGroup
ChunkGroup.description: A chunk of the page as the index embedded it, lettered in page order, with its head's words and the blocks it holds.

ChunkRun.title: ChunkRun
ChunkRun.description: A run of a block's text in a chunk: whether another chunk of the page holds it too, so that it stands in both.

CodePage.title: CodePage
CodePage.description: One file of a code work, as `open_page` serves it, with its catalog entry and its neighbours in the work's order.

CodePart.title: CodePart
CodePart.description:
A book's companion code (#12), folded into the book's row as a kept edition is into the served one (E1.a): its own
work in the search, its files opening in the code view.

CodeUnit.title: CodeUnit
CodeUnit.description: What the core's catalog says of one file's unit (`code_catalog`).

CodeWork.title: CodeWork
CodeWork.description: A code work's own page: its folders and files, each file with its catalog entry, and the core's count by category.

Companion.title: Companion
Companion.description: The book a code work accompanies, and where its record opens here (as an edition's does, E1.a).

Cost.title: Cost
Cost.description:
What every reading and judgement cost, retries included, in USD: its sum, each base's part, and each provider's over
the bases, a cost the export does not give counted as none (line 1, 19 Nov: the per-model tables go, the providers stay
in the figure's card).

Coverage.title: Coverage
Coverage.description: A PDF work's pages: how many are read, what serves the rest, and how many of those are planned, said in one line.

Edition.title: Edition
Edition.description:
One edition of a work: its label as the core names it, its format, whether it is the one served, and where its own
record opens here.

Editions.title: Editions
Editions.description: A work held in more than one edition, as its row in the list and every edition's record show it.

EpubImage.title: EpubImage
EpubImage.description:
One image where its mark stands: its path inside the EPUB, its alt text, and whether it stands inside a line of text (an
inline formula, most often) or on its own.

EpubPart.title: EpubPart
EpubPart.description: A section's text in its order: a run of text, or an image where its mark stood.

ExportStatus.title: ExportStatus
ExportStatus.description:
The background export of one knowledge base: whether one runs or waits, how many have finished (a view reloads its
data when this number moves), and the last one's error, said rather than hidden.

Figure.title: Figure
Figure.description: A headline figure: its sum over the knowledge bases it was counted in, and each base's part, the detail.

FormReading.title: FormReading
FormReading.description: One reading of the page, in the Readings or the Lab tab: time · model · cost · version · result · show.

FormRule.title: FormRule
FormRule.description: A rule a judge proposed for the reader (202.a), read-only beneath its verdict, as `ReaderRuleList` shows it.

FormVerdict.title: FormVerdict
FormVerdict.description: One verdict on a reading, in the reading's columns: time · model · cost · version · verdict · show.

Headline.title: Headline
Headline.description:
The corpus in one line: summed over the knowledge bases served, each base's part kept as the detail. The shelf's
figures are summed over the bases whose shelf is built (`shelf_left_out` names the others); the export's over the
bases served (`left_out`).

HtmlArticle.title: HtmlArticle
HtmlArticle.description:
A top unit of a work's outline whole, on one scroll (the operator, 10 Nov: a click on "Sharpe ratio" should show the whole
article): a Wikipedia article, an SRE chapter, a chapter of Lefèvre. The section asked for is the one to scroll to.

HtmlArticleEntry.title: HtmlArticleEntry
HtmlArticleEntry.description:
One place in an article's scroll, in the work's order: a section with its original and its chunks, a heading the
loader dropped as noise with its original alone, or a heading with no text of its own, which stands as a heading.

HtmlChunk.title: HtmlChunk
HtmlChunk.description:
A chunk as the index embedded it, and where its text stands in its section's text: start and end as character
offsets, None where it is not found there. `overlap` is how many of its first characters the chunk before it shares.

HtmlNode.title: HtmlNode
HtmlNode.description: A heading of the work's outline. Its label is its own section's; a heading with no text of its own has none.

HtmlSectionRow.title: HtmlSectionRow
HtmlSectionRow.description: A section in the flat table, in the work's order.

Judge.title: Judge
Judge.description: Which judge judged the reading the page shows, and with which version of its prompt (147.a).

Judgement.title: Judgement
Judgement.description:
One judge's judgement of one reading (147.a), oldest first: by which version of the judge's prompt, in which state
that version is (a prototype, the active one, retired), whether the judge was asked again, and whether it counts.

Ladder.title: Ladder
Ladder.description: A work's or the corpus's coverage ladder, and the details a fold or a card shows.

LadderState.title: LadderState
LadderState.description: A state of a work's read pages and how many are in it, as the lists count them.

LeftOut.title: LeftOut
LeftOut.description: A knowledge base a sum leaves out, and why: not served, no export, or no shelf built here.

LibrarianField.title: LibrarianField
LibrarianField.description: One argument of a tool, as its input schema gives it, for the form.

Milestone.title: Milestone
Milestone.description:
One line of the corpus's history (X1.a, line 1, 19 Nov): its date, its name, and its figures summed over the knowledge
bases it holds that this app serves, each base's part beside them. A line taken over from the person's file before
19 Nov holds both bases summed (`summed`, no parts), and is never shown under `--public-only`, as it holds licensed
counts.

OutlineUnit.title: OutlineUnit
OutlineUnit.description: One unit of a work's own order as the core cut it (decision 84.a), with its whole subtree's pages in figures.

PageLadder.title: PageLadder
PageLadder.description: A page's or a section's own ladder (the operator's V2.a, 20 Nov), and the text the librarian serves for it.

PageLink.title: PageLink
PageLink.description: Where the diagnostics shows a hit's page: the page view of an exported reading.

PageList.title: PageList
PageList.description:
The pages a filter names, each with its words in every field the Pages view narrows by (P1.a), and the order the
core gives the check states in, for the view's state facet.

PageReset.title: PageReset
PageReset.description: A person's reset of a page (191.a): the reading discarded, the text layer served until a new reading is due.

PageRung.title: PageRung
PageRung.description: One level of a page's or a section's own ladder (V2.a): whether the page reaches it, said in a line.

PersonMark.title: PersonMark
PersonMark.description:
A person's standing verdict on the reading a page shows, beside the judge's state wherever a page's state stands
(decision 166.a): accepted or rejected by the latest accept or reject that applies, as the core decides what is served
(`served_readings.human_standing`); noted where only a note applies, which never changes what is served. Its reason
and note go in the hover.

PersonVerdict.title: PersonVerdict
PersonVerdict.description:
A person's verdict on a page or one of its blocks (146.a): accept, reject or a note, with the reason given. One
given on an earlier reading of the page does not apply to the one shown, and says so.

Prefill.title: Prefill
Prefill.description:
The verdict as a proposal fills it (the operator's F1.a, 21 Nov: "fill with AI" fills the whole form): the model gives
only what needs the image, the core's fixed rules the rest (`correction_proposal.prefill`); every field stays a person's
to change, and nothing is recorded until a person records it, which `said` says beneath the form.

PromoteGiven.title: PromoteGiven
PromoteGiven.description: A recorded promotion: the reading it promoted and the export it set going.

PromoteRequest.title: PromoteRequest
PromoteRequest.description: A person's promotion of a Lab reading to the page's reading (#18): the page, the reading by its key, the reason.

Promotion.title: Promotion
Promotion.description: A person's promotion of a Lab reading to the page's reading (#18): which reading, why, by whom and when.

PromptOrigin.title: PromptOrigin
PromptOrigin.description: Who wrote a version and when, where it came from and how that is known (#18, the registry's `origin`).

PromptPart.title: PromptPart
PromptPart.description: What a prompt file is, as the registry's `parts` names it: its key, its name before the colon, the rest after.

Proposal.title: Proposal
Proposal.description:
A model's proposed correction of one block (W2.a), as the core gives it and keeps it, or why it gave none, and the
whole verdict it fills (F1.a); never recorded by itself: a person changes what they will and records it. `diff` is the block's current text against it,
word by word; `cost_usd` what it cost when it was asked, nothing again when the core answers from its store.

ProposalRequest.title: ProposalRequest
ProposalRequest.description:
A proposed correction of one block of the reading a page shows: the page by its work's id and PDF page, the block by
its id. The judge's findings on it are taken here from the page's own data, never from the browser.

ProposeState.title: ProposeState
ProposeState.description:
Whether a model's correction can be proposed here (W2.a): only where verdicts are taken and a version of the role is
active, which a person makes so after its gate; why not, in words, where it cannot.

QuotedText.title: QuotedText
QuotedText.description:
The text the search and the chat quote for a page (decision 93.a), from the core's one function for it: the served
reading as quotable text, or the cleaned text layer where the reading is not served.

ReaderRule.title: ReaderRule
ReaderRule.description:
A rule a judge proposed for the reader (decisions 195.a, 197.a: judge/4), shown read-only beneath its judgement and
never applied (202.a): its kind (a format rule, a class or an attribute of the vocabulary), the block that asked for it,
the rule in the judge's words, and the class, attribute and value it names, where it names one. The export writes ''
for a field not set; here it is None.

ReadingError.title: ReadingError
ReadingError.description:
A validator error on the reading, parted into what it names (decision 228.a, the operator on accounting p. 398: "then the only thing that still confuses me is that the error stands at the top, although I entered a correction"): the block and the line, where it
names them, so the view marks the error on its block and opens the raw text at its line. `looked` is the verdict of
the latest person's verdict that applies to the block, else to the page as a whole (`looked_at`), and `corrected`
whether a person's correction stands for the block: the view then mutes the error and says so, never hides it, as the
error is the validator's verdict on the reading, which a person's verdict does not change.

Recalled.title: Recalled
Recalled.description:
One judgement shown on the page as it judged it (decision 181.a, the operator: "you see what the old judge looked like, applied to the page"): the reading it judged, read-only, its findings on that reading's blocks, and what is shown in
one line. Never the standing view, and the view marks it so.

RouteLevel.title: RouteLevel
RouteLevel.description:
A route level, what it means in the core's words (`served_readings.ROUTE_LEVELS`), and how many of the work's pages
are served at it: the routes' one line, and their legend.

RouteRow.title: RouteRow
RouteRow.description: One route a work's pages are served by, as a person reads the routes (the operator, 10 Nov: "is this route a faulty one?"): how good it is, where the text comes from, by which reader, why, and on how many pages.

RouterPlan.title: RouterPlan
RouterPlan.description: The plan the router made, where it ran.

RunLine.title: RunLine
RunLine.description: One run as a list shows it: what was run, when, how it ended, what it cost, the batches it sent.

number.title: Number
number.description:
The level's place on the ladder, 1 to 5, before its word wherever the five levels stand (L1.a): which line of the
card a meter in the table's cell is.

share.title: Share
share.description: How much of its whole the level reaches, in whole percent (`share_of`); None where it is not measured.

Rung.title: Rung
Rung.description: One level of a ladder: how many of the whole reach it, said in a line.

Segment.title: Segment
Segment.description:
A piece of prose as the core parsed it: text, math, code, or an inline mark of its own (decision 206.a): a note's
marker (`fn`, "[4]{.fn}"), a superscript (`sup`) or a subscript (`sub`). A marker names the footnote on the same page
whose `marker` is its content (`with_notes`), and carries that note's text, so the view links the two; both None where
the page has no such note.

Series.title: Series
Series.description:
A part of a series the licensed catalog names (Y1.a, 19 Nov): one author's lecture decks, say, as parts 1 to 11.
An earlier version of a part carries its own words in `version`.

Shares.title: Shares
Shares.description: A milestone's figures for one knowledge base, as the core kept them (X1.a): None where it kept none.

ShownVerdicts.title: ShownVerdicts
ShownVerdicts.description:
The Verdicts tab's rows (decision 26): the verdicts that apply to the reading the analysis shows, what that reading
is said in a caption above them, and their count, the tab's; for a recalled trial none, and why (38.a).

Splitter.title: Splitter
Splitter.description:
How the index cuts a section into chunks, as `chunking.splitting_config` gives it: the view's legend of the overlap
says from it why a chunk repeats the end of the one before.

Stage2.title: Stage2
Stage2.description: Stage 2 of the check (146.a): the reading against the PDF's text layer, in figures and findings.

Stage2Finding.title: Stage2Finding
Stage2Finding.description: What stage 2 found comparing the reading with the PDF's text layer; an older plan gives the kind alone.

StandIn.title: StandIn
StandIn.description:
A stand-in file beside a work, which the librarian does not serve as long as the work's own text stands (the shelf's
`stand_in_of`, line 1, 20 Nov): folded into its work's row, so a work stands once, the file named in its card.

StandingCorrection.title: StandingCorrection
StandingCorrection.description:
The correction that stands for a block (decision 229.a, the operator: "what you really want to see first is the correction"): the
latest a person gave that applies to the reading shown, drawn first as the block's content, the reader's text muted
beneath it. Never served: the search and the chat quote the reading or the text layer, and the reading is unchanged.

StateCount.title: StateCount
StateCount.description:
A listed state's count, and how many of its pages a person's standing verdict accepted, rejected or noted (166.a:
"ok 399 · 1 accepted"; 211.a: "decided by a person 8 · 7 accepted · 1 noted"). `counted_states` sets them on every
count it makes; they are optional only so a count of an older shape still reads.

StatePages.title: StatePages
StatePages.description:
The pages behind one count of a unit (decision 225.a): what the count opens, in a state a person should look at or
one a person decided (`OPENED_BY_A_COUNT`).

TablePreview.title: TablePreview
TablePreview.description:
A correction's text as the table it would be, read by the core's table parser as a reading's table is (204.a);
None where it is no table, or not a clean one.

Trace.title: Trace
Trace.description: Where a reading came from: everything the export records about it except its check.

UnreadPart.title: UnreadPart
UnreadPart.description: The unread pages of a work one thing serves.

Unverifiable.title: Unverifiable
Unverifiable.description: A block stage 2 cannot check against the text layer, and why; an older plan gives the why alone.

default.why_not: Verdicts are given here only when the app was started with --allow-verdicts; it is read-only now.

VerdictForm.title: VerdictForm
VerdictForm.description:
What the page view's verdict panel offers: whether verdicts are given here at all, and if not why, the lists it
chooses from in the core's own words, each served knowledge base's export, and whether a correction can be proposed.

VerdictGiven.title: VerdictGiven
VerdictGiven.description: A recorded verdict: its id, the reading it judged, the page's route before it, and the export it set going.

VerdictRequest.title: VerdictRequest
VerdictRequest.description: A verdict on the reading a page shows: the page by its work's id and PDF page, as the views address it.

VerdictRow.title: VerdictRow
VerdictRow.description: One verdict as shown, in the Verdicts tab: standing · time · verdict · reason · about · judge · person or machine.

WaitingVerdict.title: WaitingVerdict
WaitingVerdict.description:
A verdict the pipeline database holds and the export does not hold yet (the operator's E1.a, 21 Nov: a verdict recorded
was taken for "nothing saved" while its export ran unseen): it waits for the export, and is served once that is done.

Work.title: Work
Work.description:
One work as the sources view lists it. A licensed work takes its fields from the local licensed catalog where this
machine has one (N1.a); without it, its export gives an id and a title, the PDF's stem as on the search server, and the
catalog's fields stay empty.

WorkReadings.title: WorkReadings
WorkReadings.description: A work's page readings in figures, each value as often as it occurs.
